newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for May 9.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for May 9.

text.p: All Mexican ports were open on Friday, with a cold front expected to hit the northern Gulf of Mexico later in the day, the Communications and Transport Ministry (SCT) said in its 1000 local/1500 GMT daily meteorological report.
Winds of up to 20 knots (38 km/22 miles per hour) and waves five to seven feet high were expected to hit the coast of Tamaulipas and northern Veracruz states later in the day.
Strong winds were also expected by Saturday along the Caribbean coast of Quintana Roo and Yucatan states.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Pacific Coast, Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean.
Clear skies with winds 15 to 20 knots (29 to 38 km/16 to 22 miles per hour) and waves three to six feet high along northern coastline. Winds calmer further down the coast.
Scattered rains along coasts of Jalisco, Michoacan, Oaxaca, Guerrero and Chiapas.

Winds 10 to 15 knots (19 to 29 km/11 to 16 miles per hour) with waves three to five feet high. Weak cold front expected to hit the northern gulf region later in the day or by Saturday, drawing winds of up to 20 knots.
Hot and clear to partly cloudy with winds from 20 to 30 km per hour. Winds expected to increase to 35 to 45 km per hour by Satuday.
